{{Short description|Algebraic structure}}
{{No footnotes|date=March 2023}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''quasithin group''' is a [[finite group|finite]] [[simple group]] that resembles a [[group of Lie type]] of rank at most 2 over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] of [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] 2. The classification of quasithin groups is a crucial part of the [[classification of finite simple groups]].

More precisely it is a finite simple group of [[characteristic 2 type]] and width 2. Here characteristic 2 type means that its [[centralizer]]s of [[Involution_(mathematics)#Group_theory|involutions]] resemble those of [[groups of Lie type]] over fields of characteristic 2, and the width is roughly the maximal rank of an [[abelian group]] of [[parity (mathematics)|odd]] [[order (group theory)|order]] normalizing a non-trivial 2-subgroup of ''G''. When ''G'' is a group of Lie type of characteristic 2 type, the width is usually the rank (the dimension of a [[maximal torus]] of the algebraic group).

== Classification ==
The quasithin groups were  classified in a [[List of long mathematical proofs|1221-page  paper]]  by {{harvs|txt|first1=Michael|last=Aschbacher|authorlink1=Michael Aschbacher|first2=Stephen D.|last2=Smith|year1=2004|year2=2004b}}. An earlier announcement by {{harvs|txt|first=Geoffrey|last=Mason|year=1980}} of the classification, on the basis of which the classification of finite simple groups was announced as finished in 1983, was premature as the unpublished manuscript {{harv|Mason|1981}} of his work was incomplete and contained serious gaps.

According to {{harvtxt|Aschbacher|Smith|2004b|loc=theorem 0.1.1}}, the finite simple quasithin groups of [[parity (mathematics)|even]] characteristic are given by 
*Groups of Lie type of characteristic 2 and rank 1 or 2, except that U<sub>5</sub>(''q'') only occurs for ''q'' = 4
*PSL<sub>4</sub>(2), PSL<sub>5</sub>(2), Sp<sub>6</sub>(2)
*The [[alternating group]]s on 5, 6, 8, 9 points
*PSL<sub>2</sub>(''p'') for ''p'' a [[Fermat number|Fermat]] or [[Mersenne prime]], L{{su|b=3|p=ε}}(3), L{{su|b=4|p=ε}}(3), G<sub>2</sub>(3)
*The [[Mathieu groups]] M<sub>11</sub>, M<sub>12</sub>, M<sub>22</sub>, M<sub>23</sub>, M<sub>24</sub>, The [[Janko group]]s J<sub>2</sub>, J<sub>3</sub>, J<sub>4</sub>, the [[Higman–Sims group]], the [[Held group]], and the [[Rudvalis group]].

If the condition "even characteristic" is relaxed to "even type" in the sense of the revision of the classification by [[Daniel Gorenstein]], [[Richard Lyons (mathematician)|Richard Lyons]], and [[Ronald Solomon]], then the only extra group that appears is the [[Janko group J1]].
